reasons: Only one of the seven tools has detail data, so most links from the tools list fail.
Request Demo and Schedule Consultation buttons have no action.
Results and claims are hardcoded and not backed by anything visible in the code.
No tests are visible in this file.

terms.meaning: a reusable building block of a web page, written as a function that describes what to show
a web address pattern where one part, here the tool id, changes which content the page shows
values handed to a component from outside, such as the tool id here
a helper package that makes elements fade or slide smoothly instead of appearing instantly
a package that supplies small standard pictures used on buttons and headings

used_by: The Next.js router, for web addresses starting with /tools/ followed by a tool id (not imported by another file in this packet)

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports and browser setup
sections.what: Loads the animation library, the link helper, and the icons this page uses, and marks the file to run in the visitor's browser.
sections.why: Likely reason: the page uses animations and clickable links, which need to run in the browser.
sections.watch_out: Any new icon used on this page must also be added to this import list, or the page will fail to load.

sections.name: toolDetails
sections.title: Built-in data for the AI Strategy Advisor
sections.what: Holds all the text, features, use cases, method steps, outcomes, and pricing for the AI Strategy Advisor, keyed by its id. It is the only tool with details.
sections.why: The code comment says this is a stand-in for a database, and says more tools should be added here.
sections.watch_out: Each new tool needs every field this page displays, or that part of the page will be empty or break; pricing is stored but never shown.

sections.name: ToolDetailPage (part 1)
sections.title: Lookup, not-found message, and header
sections.what: Finds the tool matching the web address. If none matches, it shows a Tool not found message with a button back to the tools list. Otherwise it draws the top bar with a back link and the tool's icon, category, name, and tagline.
sections.why: Keeps the page from crashing on an unknown id and gives the visitor a way back.
sections.watch_out: The lookup uses the raw id from the web address, so a new id in the data must match the address exactly, including capital letters.

sections.name: ToolDetailPage (part 2)
sections.title: Description, buttons, and quick stats
sections.what: Shows the long description and two buttons: Discuss in AI Console opens the chat page, and Request Demo does nothing yet. Below, three summary tiles show the pilot length, the number of outcomes counted from the list, and a fixed 100 percent Human Oversight figure.
sections.why: Likely reason: the console button is the main way into a conversation. Reason for the fixed 100 percent figure not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: Request Demo has no click action, so a visitor who presses it gets no response.

sections.name: ToolDetailPage (part 3)
sections.title: Feature cards and use case cards
sections.what: Lists each key feature in a card with a sparkle icon, then lists each real-world use case with its challenge, solution, and outcome side by side.
sections.why: Shows repeated items in a consistent card layout, so adding an item to the data adds a card without changing the layout.
sections.watch_out: Cards are identified by their title text, so two items with the same title would confuse the page.

sections.name: ToolDetailPage (part 4)
sections.title: Method steps and expected outcomes
sections.what: Shows the numbered methodology steps in order, then a grid of expected outcomes, each with a check mark.
sections.why: Gives the visitor a quick picture of how the work is done and what they receive.
sections.watch_out: Steps and outcomes are identified by their text, so repeated entries in the same list can cause display problems.

sections.name: ToolDetailPage (part 5)
sections.title: Closing call to action
sections.what: Final banner with a Start in AI Console button that opens the chat page, and a Schedule Consultation button that does nothing yet.
sections.why: Repeats the main next step at the bottom so a visitor who has read everything can act right away.
sections.watch_out: Schedule Consultation has no click action, the same as Request Demo above it.

summary: Detail page for one AI tool, showing its header, quick stats, features, use cases, method steps, outcomes, and a closing call to action, chosen by the tool id in the web address.
purpose: Gives a visitor a full description of a single tool. The text and numbers are stored inside this file rather than loaded from a database.
why: Likely reason: the code comment says the data would normally come from a database or API, so this file is an early stand-in. Reason for the page layout not stated in the code.
how: Reads the tool id from the web address and looks it up in the built-in list. If nothing matches, it shows a Tool not found message with a link back. If it matches, it draws the page sections from top to bottom, with fade-in animations as the visitor scrolls.
inputs: The tool id from the web address (params.id), and the toolDetails list defined in this file.
outputs: A web page: either a not-found message with a Back to Tools button, or the full detail page for the matching tool.
risks: Only the AI Strategy Advisor has details, but the tools list page has six other tools that link here, so those links show Tool not found. The 15 percent cost reduction and 100 percent Human Oversight figure are fixed text, not measured results. The Request Demo and Schedule Consultation buttons have no click action. The pricing values are defined but never shown.
debug: If a tool page says not found, check that the id in the web address matches a key in toolDetails exactly. If text is missing from a section, check the matching field in toolDetails. If a button does nothing, that is expected because no action is attached. To confirm the page works, open the address for the ai-strategy-advisor tool.
